description.narrative: The outcome of the project is to provide an enabling environment for industrial symbiosis to protect natural resources through better use of these resources, to improve human and environmental health through decreasing the amount of industrial waste through innovative, environment-friendly and sustainable synergistic industrial symbiosis links and to diversify supply-chain relations in the industry to increase resilience to disasters. sector.narrative: Eradicate poverty in all its forms and dimensions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative: 1.2. Updating information with regards to available platforms and similar best practices around the world for industrial symbiosis will be analysed and elaborately reviewed. 1.3 Updating the methodology will be developed to establish the best suitable platform for Izmir Region’s industrial symbiosis programme. 1.4. Developing/Procuring the Software Structure to Support IS Programme. 1.5. Updating the governance mechanism for Izmir Region’s industrial symbiosis programme. 1.6. Need Assessment. 2.3. Supporting 7 PhD thesis in the field of industrial symbiosis in Izmir Region with the partnership of university, government, and private sector. 2.4. Supporting academic studies between academics at the identified universities and private sector to support private sector and university partnerships. 3.1. Carrying out a legal framework analysis (national, international, EU) within the scope of industrial symbiosis. 3.2. Carrying out a legal gap analysis. 3.3. Conducting a series of workshops to identify legal gaps in industrial symbiosis implementation with central and provincial governmental institutions, private sector and universities. 3.4. Preparation of policy suggestions for industrial symbiosis. 3.5. Conducting a feasibility study for end-of-waste criteria in three identified sectors. 3.6. Finalizing needs assessment study. 3.7. Sectoral IS Report in Izmir Region 4.1. Training private sector, central and provincial government institutions, universities, municipalities on industrial symbiosis and international best practices. 4.2. Identifying the model for Resource Efficiency Centers and training the personnel in these centers. 4.3. Carrying out synergy workshops in the region, with no limitations on the scale of OIZ or SME or industry or sector. 4.4. Identifying potential options for industrial symbiosis in the field of energy, raw materials, waste, water, human resources, etc.

1.2. A summary report on similar platforms and best practices are prepared to provide international know-how in this field. 1.3. A summary report on methodology and platform is prepared by the national consultant and reviewed by the Chief Technical Advisor (CTA). A workshop on the industrial symbiosis management model for the Izmir region has been held. The methodology will be continuously updated by the project team and the CTA according to the progress of the project and lessons learned. 1.4. It has been determined that using an international available software during the trainings and synergy workshops would be advantageous. In the meantime, a national software structure would be developed and the needs of the system to be identified and necessary information for the structure to be provided through results from realized workshops and trainings. 1.5. Updating the governance mechanism for Izmir Region’s industrial symbiosis programme is planned to be updated accordingly during the project cycle to find out the best mechanism for the industrial symbiosis programme in Izmir. 1.6. It has been determined that needs assessment is no longer needed since the draft needs assessment document had already been realized before the establishment of the project by the implementing partner IZKA through the workshops in the field. 2.3. PMU visited TÜBITAK representatives in Ankara in February 2022 and negotiated regarding the general criteria, scholarship amount, and the details of the scholarship programme call. Following the visit, a Letter of Agreement (LoA) and project details are prepared and signed by both parties in March 2022. The same month, TÜBITAK-BIDEB issued the first scholarship call. 5 candidates were shortlisted in May 2022 and the selection, and 2 candidates were met the criteria for the scholarship. The second round of the call is published for between the October and November. Evaluation process of the candidates continues. 2.4. PMU plans to have potential matches between academics and the private sector with the initiated synergy workshops both in 2022 and 2023. Additionally, Waste to value workshops will be initiated. During this workshop, a small group of academicians will present up to date innovations and end of waste criteria on a chosen topic defined by the project team to a selected group of academicians and R&D representatives from the industry. The first workshop will be related to aluminum and aluminum alloy scrap. This activity is to be updated during the project cycle. 3.1. Draft legal framework analysis within the industrial symbiosis is completed. IC is working on the feedbacks from the PMU to finalize it. 3.2. PMU conducted meetings with the national project consultant, national project consultant is currently working on the legal gap analysis report. 3.3. PMU plans to hold series of workshops following the completion of legal framework and legal gap analysis documents. These workshops will be realized in 2023. 3.4. Preparation of Legal Policy Recommendation Document is planned for 2023. 3.5. PMU plans to hold series of Waste-to-Value Workshops, starting with the aliminum sector, in 2023. 3.6. It has been determined that needs assessment is no longer needed within the scope of the project. 3.7. The activities are initiated for Sectoral Industrial Symbiosis Report for Izmir Region . 4.1. First training of trainees is realized in May 2022. Moderation Training is realized in July 2022. 20 people were trained within the scope of this activity. 4.2. PMU conducted meetings with the national consultant and the activities are initiated for Izmir Resource Efficiency Center Feasibility Report. 4.3. First two synergy workshops are conducted between the dates of 5-6 July 2022 and second two synergy workshops are conducted between the dates of 23-24 November 2022. 4.4. The preparation activities are initiated for Potential Industrial Symbiosis Possibilities .

Inception Period 0.1 Project team will be established and Project Office will be prepared. 0.2 Institutional Identity for the Project will be prepared. 0.3 Communication and Visibility activities will be conducted. 0.4 Consultants will be recruited. 0.5 PMU meetings and Project Steering Committee will be held. Implementation Period 1.1. Updating Turkey’s experience on industrial symbiosis through literature review, synergy development with previous and already existing initiatives will be searched and made available as available resource documents. 1.2. Updating information with regards to available platforms and similar best practices around the world for industrial symbiosis will be analysed and elaborately reviewed. 1.3 Updating the methodology will be developed to establish the best suitable platform for Izmir Region’s industrial symbiosis programme. 2.1. Identifying partners such as universities, research institutions that would foster industrial symbiosis initiatives in technical terms. 2.2. Identifying private sector partners, that are voluntary for industrial symbiosis, and would act like anchor tenant for IRISP, such as iron and steel industry in Aliaga Region. 2.3. Supporting 7 PhD thesis in the field of industrial symbiosis in Izmir Region with the partnership of university, government, and private sector.

Inception Period 0.1 The human resources were deployed, and the project office was prepared. A project coordination unit (PCU) which compose of the UNDP and IZKA staff specifically for this project was established. A detailed workplan for the first year was prepared. A kick-off meeting and the launch event of the project was conducted. 0.2 A communication strategy and implementation were prepared for the project to outline the target group of the project, the tone of communication, creation of institutional identity, brand management for the project including web site, logo, etc. Project video and first two newsletter was prepared. The project website is established. 0.3 Communication and Visibility activities are (i) Project Visibility Materials (vacuum flask, cloth bag and erasable notebook) are designed, manufactured, and shared with the Project Team both in Ankara and Izmir. All materials either have projects logo and projects partners logo with the QR code of project web site on them or both. (ii) Project web site has been published. (iii) Project video and newsletters have been prepared and published on the web site. (iv) Summary Report for Industrial Symbiosis Background in Turkey has prepared and revised. 0.4 Contracts signed with the Chief Technical Advisor and wsth the National Consultant. 0.5 Two PMU meetings and first Project Steering Committee was held. Implementation Period 1.1. A Draft Summary Report and Final Summary Report on review of existing literature on Turkey’s up to date experience in industrial symbiosis including literature review were prepared to introduce industrial symbiosis concept, its evolution history in the world and what has been done so far in Turkey. The report also has a section for lessons learnt from so far implemented projects and recommendations for a more successful implementation for the PMU. 1.2. A Draft Summary Report and Final Summary Report on review of existing platforms internationally was prepared to analyse the functioning mechanisms, outputs, and successful cases to be able to provide an international know-how in this field. Several meetings are conducted so far, for this activity with PMU, CTA, and National Consultant. This activity is in progress and will be finalized in 2022. 1.3 A platform and methodology report were outlined to analyse different approaches and discusses advantages and disadvantages of these approaches and finally proposes a methodology for Turkey’s industrial symbiosis programme. Several meetings are conducted so far, for this activity with PMU, CTA, and National Consultant for Component 1. This activity is in progress and will be finalized in 2022. 2.1. Preparation of the list of partners in academics present with Expression of their interest in taking part in this Industrial Symbiosis Programme is initiated. 2.2. The team was already visited Atatürk OIZ, Aliaga OIZ, Menemen Plastik Specialized OIZ, Tire OIZ, Pancar OIZ, Aegean Free Zone, Izmir Bilimpark during the fieldwork that started with the Aegean Region Chamber of Industry, Izmir Chamber of Commerce, Izmir Commodity Exchange, and Aegean Exporters Association. Preparation of the list of private sectors/industries is present with Expression of their interest in taking part in this Industrial Symbiosis Programme is initiated. 2.3. Several meetings are conducted so far, for this activity with TUBITAK for the cooperation. TUBITAK verbally agreed on the details of the programme. A Project Cooperation Agreement is being drafted to be made between TUBITAK and UNDP. This activity is in progress and will be finalized in 2022.
